paths: Actual dating sign-in -> separate loopback consent -> valid S256 code exchange -> default server identity verifier; private first setup persists across reload without a second token exchange or profile storage in the browser.
A second isolated browser context starts signed out, obtains its own PKCE session and restores the same saved account from SQLite without copying browser credentials or resubmitting profile data.
A real access_denied callback removes the pending transaction and OAuth URL fields, shows cancellation, and creates no token request or account view.
A mismatched-state callback is cleaned and rejected before token exchange; an explicit new sign-in creates a fresh PKCE transaction and restores the account successfully.
Replaying an already-consumed callback makes no second token request and exposes no profile in the rejected page; a clean reload uses the still-valid prior account session.
